'''Aaron Gibson''' (born September 27, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Detroit Lions]], [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Chicago Bears]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Wisconsin]]. Gibson holds the record for heaviest NFL player ever. He was listed at 410 lbs by the Cowboys in 2002.<ref name="weight"/>

==Early life==
Gibson attended [[Decatur Central High School]], where he [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[American football|football]] and [[track and field|track]]. He weighed over 350 lbs in high school.<ref name="weight">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-palm-beach-post/173339616/|title=Pressure to grow burdened Gibson |last=Frias |first=Carlos |date=October 29, 2006 |newspaper=Palm Beach Post}}</ref>

He was a two-way player. As a senior, he was a first-team All-state selection and was named as a Top 33 Pick by the Bloomington Herald-Times. As a [[defensive tackle]], he had 8 fumble recoveries and 11 passes defensed.

==College career==
Gibson accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Wisconsin]]. He didn't play in his freshman year because of failing to meet the requirements of [[Proposition 48 (NCAA)|Proposition 48]]. The next year, he was a reserve [[right tackle]] behind [[All-American]] [[Jerry Wunsch]] and was used primarily as a blocking [[tight end]], after making his debut in the fifth game against [[Ohio State University]].<ref name="sportsillustrated"/>

As a junior in 1997, he became the starter at [[right tackle]]. He spent two seasons blocking for [[Heisman Trophy]] winner [[Ron Dayne]], who set the NCAA Division I career rushing
record (6,397 yards) in 1999.

As a senior in 1998, Gibson was recognized as a consensus first-team [[All-American]], after having been named to the first-teams of the Football Writers Association, American Football Coaches Association, and the ''Football News'' and the Walter Camp Foundation. He was also a unanimous first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] selection. He was the first player in school history to be named a finalist for the [[Lombardi Award]] and [[Outland Trophy]] awards.

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
In the 1999 [[NFL Scouting Combine]], Gibson ran the [[40-yard dash]] in 5.3 seconds.<ref name="sportsillustrated">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1999/02/22/256260/big-cheese-the-badgers-aaron-gibson-pruned-his-weight-to-371-and-blossomed-into-a-bulldozer-of-a-blocker-who-probably-will-be-the-first-lineman-taken-in-the-nfl-draft |title=Big Cheese The Badgers Aaron Gibson Pruned His Weight To 371 And Blossomed Into A Bulldozer Of A Blocker Who Probably Will Be The First Lineman Taken In The NFL Draft |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=April 1999 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was described as "a proto-type right tackle in the NFL," for having "a huge body with big legs and a gigantic chest".<ref name="sportsillustrated"/>

===Detroit Lions===
Gibson was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[1999 National Football League Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=March 28, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was expected to be the starting [[right tackle]] as a rookie, but suffered a left shoulder injury in an April post-draft minicamp and was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].

The following season, he started the first 10 games at [[right tackle]], until suffering a right shoulder injury (torn posterior subluxation) and being placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on December 4. In [[2001 Detroit Lions season|2001]], he started five of the first six games of the season, before being waived on October 30.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2001/10/31/lions-waive-99-top-pick-gibson/ | title=Lions waive '99 top pick Gibson | date=October 31, 2001 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On October 31, 2001, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] but played only in the season finale. In 2002, Gibson had the distinction of becoming the NFL's first player to be officially listed at {{convert|400|lb|kg|0|disp=or}}.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2002/07/28/nfl-lineman-comes-up-big-no-fat-lies/ | title=NFL lineman comes up big: no fat lies | date=July 28, 2002 | access-date=February 19, 2018 | archive-date=September 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930092848/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2002-07-28/sports/0207280330_1_gibson-ted-washington-heaviest-player | url-status=live }}</ref> Gibson was limited by a knee injury in [[training camp]] and eventually released on September 18, 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2002 |title=Cowboys release Gibson |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=20020919&id=CxZZAAAAIBAJ&sjid=bkYNAAAAIBAJ&pg=5646,4038817&hl=es |access-date=February 19, 2018 |website=The Victoria Advocate|via=Google News}}</ref> He holds the record for heaviest NFL player ever.<ref name="weight"/> He was listed at 410 lbs, by the Cowboys in 2002.<ref name="weight"/>

===Chicago Bears===
On November 26, 2002, he was signed by the [[Chicago Bears]] as a [[free agent]] to replace an injured [[Marc Colombo]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2002/11/27/big-deal-bears-bring-in-gibson/ | title=Big deal: Bears bring in Gibson | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> In 2003, he had his most consistent professional season, starting at [[right tackle]] in all sixteen games with the Bears, after Colombo was lost for the year when he was placed on the Physically Unable to Perform list. In 2004, he played four games (three starts) and was declared inactive in 10. It would be the last season in which he made an appearance in a regular season NFL game.

===Buffalo Bills===
On April 5, 2006, Gibson signed with the Buffalo Bills as a [[free agent]]. He was cut on August 28.

===Austin Wranglers===
On January 24, [[2007 Arena Football League season|2007]], he was signed by the [[Austin Wranglers]] of the [[Arena Football League]].<ref name="wranglers">{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=104 |title=Aaron Gibson |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On April 4, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]]. On May 5, he was activated. He played in eleven games and had 3 tackles for the season.<ref name="wranglers"/>

===Utah Blaze===
On July 30, 2007, Gibson was traded along with [[defensive line]]man Rob Schroeder to the [[Utah Blaze]] in exchange for past considerations.<ref name="wranglers"/>

===Dallas Desperados===
On October 12, 2007, he was traded to the [[Dallas Desperados]] in exchange for [[offensive line]]man [[Devin Wyman]] and future considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=7971 |title=Blaze trade Gibson to Dallas |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=October 12, 2007|access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On February 22, [[2008 Arena Football League season|2008]], Gibson was released by the Desperados, owned by [[Jerry Jones]], who also owned [[history of the Dallas Cowboys|the Dallas Cowboys]], where Gibson had previously played.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=8334 |title=Desperados release eight, re-sign Jones |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Gladiators===
On March 13, [[2008 Arena Football League season|2008]], he was signed by the [[Cleveland Gladiators]] of the AFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=8478 |title=Gladiators Sign Aaron Gibson |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On May 22, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].

===Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings===
On March 22, [[2010 Arena Football League season|2010]], he was assigned to the [[Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings]] of the AFL.<ref name="wings">{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=141 |title=Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings Team Roster |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On August 9, he was suspended by the team.<ref name="wings"/> He was not re-signed after the season.
